notes.example:
/wɪˈðaʊt ˈeni ˈhɪkʌps/
Formalnie (OET): without any complications / without any difficulties

We managed to stent the IVC without any hiccups.
The handover went without any hiccups — very smooth.
The transfer was completed without any hiccups, thankfully.

/tə hænd ˈsʌmwʌn ˈəʊvə/
Formalnie (OET): to transfer care of / to formally transfer to the care of

I'll hand him over to the ward team now.
She was handed over to the night team at ten o'clock.
Make sure you hand the patient over properly before you leave.

/ɒbz/
Formalnie (OET): vital signs / physiological observations / clinical observations

Keep an eye on his obs — NEWS2 is creeping up.
Her obs have been stable all morning.
Can you do his obs again? I'm not happy with that blood pressure.

/tə fɑːst træk/
Formalnie (OET): to expedite / to prioritise urgently

We need to fast-track a CT scan right away.
She was fast-tracked to the cardiac unit given her presentation.
Can we fast-track this referral? I'm worried about the timeline.

/tə ruːl aʊt/
Formalnie (OET): to exclude

We need to rule out a bleed before giving pain relief.
The CT was requested to rule out pulmonary embolism.
I'd like to rule out infection before we proceed.

/tə kənˈsent ə ˈpeɪʃənt/
Formalnie (OET): to obtain the patient's informed consent

I just need to consent the patient in bay three.
Has she been consented for the procedure?
Could you consent Mr Johnson while I scrub in?

/ˈklɒtɪŋ ˈprəʊfaɪl/
Formalnie (OET): coagulation screen / coagulation profile

We need to check his clotting profile before booking.
Her clotting profile came back deranged — hold the procedure.
Send a clotting profile along with the routine bloods.

/tə bliːp ˈsʌmwʌn/
Formalnie (OET): to contact / to page

Can you bleep the on-call reg, please?
I've been bleeped three times in the last hour.
Bleep the anaesthetist — we may need their input.

/tə teɪk blʌdz/
Formalnie (OET): to obtain blood samples / to collect blood specimens

The nurse will take bloods first thing in the morning.
I've asked the FY1 to take bloods before the ward round.
We'll take bloods on admission and repeat at six hours.

/tə ˈeskəleɪt/
Formalnie (OET): to escalate to a senior clinician / to seek senior review

If his obs deteriorate, escalate to the registrar.
I escalated to the consultant when I wasn't happy with the progress.
Don't hesitate to escalate if you're concerned — that's what we're here for.

/nɪl baɪ maʊθ/
Formalnie (OET): fasting / no oral intake / restricted to nil orally

Keep him nil by mouth from midnight.
She's been nil by mouth since eight this morning.
Make sure the NBM sign is clearly visible above the bed.

notes.front: to write someone up (for a drug)
notes.back: zaordynować lek / wpisać do karty zleceń
notes.example:
/tə raɪt ˈsʌmwʌn ʌp/
Formalnie (OET): to prescribe / to chart a medication

I'll write him up for some analgesia.
Can you write her up for antiemetics? She's quite nauseated.
He's already been written up for heparin — check the drug chart.

/tə flæɡ ˈsʌmθɪŋ ʌp/
Formalnie (OET): to highlight / to draw attention to / to raise

The nurse flagged up that his urine output had dropped significantly.
I wanted to flag up a safeguarding concern before discharge.
Can you flag this up at the MDT? I think it needs discussing.

notes.back: kwalifikować się do wypisu / być gotowym do domu
notes.example:
/tə biː fɪt fə dɪsˈtʃɑːdʒ/
Formalnie (OET): medically optimised for discharge / suitable for discharge

She's medically fit for discharge, but we're waiting on social care.
He's been fit for discharge since yesterday — it's a bed management issue.
We'll review her this afternoon and decide if she's fit for discharge.

/tə pʊt ˈsʌmθɪŋ ɒn həʊld/
Formalnie (OET): to defer / to postpone / to suspend

We've put the procedure on hold until his INR comes down.
The discharge has been put on hold pending the social work assessment.
Let's put that on hold and revisit it after the weekend.

/tə pʊt ɪn ə rɪˈfɜːrəl/
Formalnie (OET): to submit a referral / to make a referral

I'll put in a referral to vascular surgery today.
The GP has already put in a referral — we're waiting for the appointment.
Could you put in an urgent referral to oncology?

/tə biː ɒn kɔːl/
Formalnie (OET): to be the on-call clinician / to be covering out-of-hours

Who's on call tonight — do you know?
I was on call all weekend and barely slept.
The on-call registrar dealt with it overnight.

/tə tʃeɪs ə rɪˈzʌlt/
Formalnie (OET): to follow up on / to request an update on

Can you chase that CT result? It was requested three hours ago.
I've been chasing the biopsy result all week.
Chase the microbiology result — we need it before we can discharge.

/tə kʌm ɒf/
Formalnie (OET): to discontinue / to withdraw

He came off warfarin two weeks before the procedure.
She's been trying to come off the antidepressants gradually.
We'll come off the IV antibiotics once he can tolerate oral.

notes.back: wracać do zdrowia / być na dobrej drodze
notes.example:
/tə biː ɒn ðə mend/
Formalnie (OET): to be recovering / to be improving / to be making good progress

Good news — he's on the mend and should be home by Friday.
She's definitely on the mend; her obs have been stable all day.
It's early days, but he's on the mend.

/tə teɪk ə ˈhɪstri/
Formalnie (OET): to obtain a clinical history / to conduct a clinical assessment

Has anyone taken a full history from her yet?
I'll take a history while you set up the trolley.
The student took a thorough history — very impressive.

/ɒn ðə wɔːd raʊnd/
Formalnie (OET): during the daily clinical review / at the morning review

We'll discuss his management on the ward round tomorrow morning.
The consultant reviewed all twelve patients on the ward round.
I'll present the new admission on the ward round.

notes.back: być na sali operacyjnej / w trakcie zabiegu
notes.example:
/tə biː ɪn ˈθɪətə/
Formalnie (OET): to be performing a procedure / to be in the operating theatre

The consultant is in theatre until three — bleep the registrar instead.
I'll be in theatre all morning; can someone cover my bleep?
She's been in theatre since seven — it's a long case.

/tə liˈeɪz/
Formalnie (OET): to coordinate with / to collaborate with / to work in conjunction with

Please liaise with the community nurse before we discharge her.
I've been liaising with the social work team about his housing situation.
Could you liaise with pharmacy regarding the new prescription?

notes.front: to step down (to a lower level of care)
notes.back: przenieść na oddział o niższym stopniu opieki
notes.example:
/tə step daʊn/
Formalnie (OET): to de-escalate care / to transfer to a lower level of care

He's stable enough to step down from HDU to the general ward.
We'll step down the oxygen support gradually over the next 24 hours.
Once she's stepped down, we can start planning discharge.

notes.front: to keep someone in the loop
notes.example:
/tə kiːp ˈsʌmwʌn ɪn ðə luːp/
Formalnie (OET): to keep someone informed / to update someone regularly

Keep the family in the loop — they're very anxious.
Please keep me in the loop if anything changes overnight.
The GP should be kept in the loop throughout the admission.

/tə ɡəʊ ˈəʊvə ðə nəʊts/
Formalnie (OET): to review the documentation / to go through the clinical records

I'll go over the notes before the ward round tomorrow.
Have you had a chance to go over her notes from the last admission?
Let me go over the notes — I wasn't here when she came in.

notes.front: to be under the care of
notes.example:
/tə biː ˈʌndə ðə keər ɒv/
Formalnie (OET): to be managed by / to be under the supervision of

She is currently under the care of the hepatology team.
He was under the care of cardiology during his last admission.
The patient will remain under the care of the surgical team until discharge.

/tə rɪˈvjuː ə ˈpeɪʃənt/
Formalnie (OET): to assess / to re-evaluate / to conduct a clinical review of

Can you review the patient in bay two? I'm not happy with her progress.
I've asked the registrar to review him before we make a decision.
She was reviewed by the medical team and found to be improving.

/tə teɪk ˈəʊvə/
Formalnie (OET): to assume responsibility for / to take charge of

I'll take over from you at eight — go home and get some rest.
The night team will take over from us at ten.
She took over the case when the consultant was called away.
